decision_rule: An item is approved only when every independent reviewer approves it. One written objection from one reviewer withholds approval and leaves the item a candidate. No producer of an item reviewed that item, and this record does not overturn a verdict.
what_an_approval_permits: An approved row may be named by a host manifest and served by a host whose licence policy accepts the exact licence the item declares. Approval grants no effect, no network access, no spending and no model authority.
what_a_rejection_records: A rejected row stays a candidate with its reason. It is not deleted, not edited to pass, and not written into any host manifest. It may be resubmitted after the reason is answered, which needs a new review.

decisions.reason: Reviewer three (adversarial lens) — independent review, not the producer of any item: It declares no effect and gives no authority statement, yet its title, its trigger (use it when a model is asked the same kind of question many times) and its step 6 stride order put the reader at the point of issuing many model calls, which need network access, a credential and money; its sibling escalate_uncertain_values_with_candidates carries the exact missing sentence (the request makes no call, building it grants nothing and spends nothing), so with declared_effects empty this item is offered to a step holding zero authority.

Reviewer one (correctness and usefulness lens), Claude Opus 5: The join advice itself is correct, but the item declares `license: "unknown"` over four unreviewed model-generated source statements, and `load_host_manifest` refuses it with `item_license_unknown` before registration while `HostLicensePolicy` refuses any host policy that lists `unknown`, so it can never be served and its rights are unsettled; settle the rights or rewrite it from MIT material and resubmit.

Reviewer two — provenance, licence and safety: It declares the licence "unknown" with state needs_review over four model-generated statements (string-foundry-20260823, deepseek-v4-flash:0731) that its own body says no person has reviewed, so no rights determination exists and load_host_manifest refuses it as item_license_unknown before registration — a state HostLicensePolicy forbids any host from listing as accepted.

Reviewer three (adversarial lens) — independent review, not the producer of any item: It declares the licence unknown, which _license_state maps to item_license_unknown before registration, so no host policy can accept it and a manifest carrying it makes load_host_manifest raise and refuses all 47 other items with it; its only source is four unreviewed model-generated statements in src/loop_engine/governance/candidates/part-00000.jsonl, so nothing establishes the rights in the text and approving the content would not make it servable.

Reviewer one (correctness and usefulness lens), Claude Opus 5: The idempotence and partition-swap advice itself is correct, but the item declares `license: "unknown"` over four unreviewed model-generated source statements, and `load_host_manifest` refuses it with `item_license_unknown` before registration while `HostLicensePolicy` refuses any host policy that lists `unknown`, so it can never be served and its rights are unsettled; settle the rights or rewrite it from MIT material and resubmit.

Reviewer two — provenance, licence and safety: Same unreviewed model-generated provenance and "unknown" licence, refused as item_license_unknown before registration; it additionally declares only reads_fs while its steps write a staging partition, swap it into production and rerun each step to compare checksums, so its write and process effects are undeclared.

Reviewer three (adversarial lens) — independent review, not the producer of any item: Same defect as check_a_table_join_before_trusting_it: licence unknown, refused by the loader with item_license_unknown before its body is opened and aborting the whole manifest load, and compiled from the same four unreviewed model-generated statements, so its rights must be settled or the item rewritten from material whose licence is known before any approval can matter.

Reviewer two — provenance, licence and safety: Its declared effects are writes_fs alone, but step 9 and the check "The structure check passes" require executing integrations/tests/check_integrations.py and reading back every generated manifest and skill file, so spawns_process and reads_fs are undeclared for the same kind of work that test_driven_change_red_green_refactor declares all three for, and because harness_intelligence.visibility gates offering on declared_effects the item would be handed to a step that holds no execution authority at all.

Reviewer three (adversarial lens) — independent review, not the producer of any item: A near duplicate of orient_on_a_task_and_write_its_contracts, which covers the same moment and produces an artifact instead of a list; eleven of its thirteen questions restate content already owned by six other items in this set and three of them cite the identical question forms (acceptance_inversion with verify_the_requested_output, whose step 1 is the same sentence; state_the_unknowns with resolve_missing_information; stakeholder_view with hand_over_a_result_its_consumer_can_use), leaving only the failure map and second order questions unique, which does not earn a separate item in a catalogue whose value is that a search returns the one right item.

Reviewer three (adversarial lens) — independent review, not the producer of any item: The title and framing promise that generated files holding secrets are refused, but the rule is four narrow shapes (verified in solution_export.py line 43: sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}, AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}, a bearer header, a private key header) that do not match sk_live_, ghp_, AIza or a JWT, and nothing in the body says the list is a floor rather than coverage, so an agent packaging a file containing this repository's own live Stripe key shape sees the check pass and publishes it.
